title: Pennsieve app manifest (app.yml)
description: What a Pennsieve app is and needs: its metadata, how it runs, its parameters, and what goes in and comes out. Kept at the root of the app's repository as app.yml and read when a release is registered. Version 1 grows only by optional, backward-compatible additions; a breaking change is a new major version (v2.json). Field names follow CodeMeta/schema.org, Boutiques and CWL where they overlap, so a manifest can be translated to them.

$schema.description: The schema this file follows. Prefer the editor comment `# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://schemas.pennsieve.io/app-manifest/v1.json` on the first line.

schemaVersion.description: The manifest format version the file was written for, e.g. "1.0". Informational.

parameters.description: The app's parameters, which a workflow sets per step.

outputs.description: What the app writes. With one output it is the whole of OUTPUT_DIR; with two or more, each is written to its own folder, OUTPUT_DIR/<name>/, so a workflow can route each output on its own (names must then be folder-safe).

commandArguments.description: Deprecated and not read from app.yml.

application.description: What the app is (CodeMeta/schema.org SoftwareSourceCode terms). Its version comes from the release tag, its repository from where it's registered, and its license from the repository's LICENSE file, so none of those are declared here.

id.description: An identifier the author chooses for the app. Optional; Pennsieve identifies an app by its repository.

description.description: What the app does, in a sentence or two.

type.description: The role the app plays in a workflow. Only "processor" today.

version.description: Optional and informational: the version Pennsieve shows is the release tag.

tags.description: Keywords (schema.org keywords) that say what the app is for, e.g. eeg, spikes, visualization. A known subject or task places the app in the Gallery's colours and filters.

categories.description: Deprecated: use tags. Older manifests' categories are read as tags.

orcid.description: Their ORCID iD, e.g. 0000-0002-1825-0097 (the https://orcid.org/ form is accepted too).

runtime.description: How the app runs: its size, the compute it runs on, its time limit, and whether it's a live session.

cpu.description: CPU units (1024 = 1 vCPU). Optional; the platform picks a default.

memory.description: Memory in MiB. Optional; the platform picks a default.

computeTypes.description: The compute the app can run on: standard (a container), lambda, or gpu. Default: [standard].

timeoutSeconds.description: How long a run may take before it's stopped.

llm.description: The app calls language models through Pennsieve (the LLM governor): its runs get the LLM proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) and LLM_GOVERNOR_FUNCTION_NAME, with usage metered against the workspace's budget. Apps that don't declare it run without them. Default: false.

interactive.description: A live session a person works in, rather than a batch step: the workflow waits while it runs. Default: false.

sessionType.description: The kind of live session. "jupyter" is a Jupyter notebook. Needs interactive: true.

kernel.description: A Jupyter notebook's language. Needs sessionType: jupyter.

parameter.description: One parameter. Types are JSON Schema's; they correspond to Boutiques String/Number/Flag and CWL string/float/int/boolean. A choice is a string (or number) with validValues.

name.description: The name the app reads it by (its environment variable).

type.description: string, number, integer or boolean. Default: string.

required.description: Whether a run must set it. Default: required when it has no defaultValue.

defaultValue.description: The value used when a run doesn't set one.

validValues.description: The values it may take, making it a choice.

min.description: For a number or integer: the smallest value.

max.description: For a number or integer: the largest value.

structureRef.description: A structure id from the Pennsieve format registry, optionally with a version (bids, bids@1.9), or a link to a specification.

port.description: An input or output. Without mediaTypes, formats or conformsTo it accepts any file.

allOf.$comment: Folders of a format need the format: container directory without conformsTo names at least one media type.

name.description: Its name: an identifier, e.g. study. With placement subfolder it is also the input's folder name.

mediaTypes.description: The MIME types it takes or makes, e.g. application/x-rds.

formats.description: EDAM format identifiers (https://edamontology.org/page), for scientific formats without a MIME type, e.g. format_3590 (HDF5) or http://edamontology.org/format_3549 (NIfTI-1). EDAM has no id for some formats (EDF, NWB, MEF3); use mediaTypes for those.

container.description: How folder-format items (a registry format with kind directory, such as OME-Zarr or MEF3) are given to the app, or written by it. directory: each item as a plain folder with the format's folder ending (e.g. brain-01.ome.zarr/, session.mefd/); an input can take several, so expect one or more folders. file: each item as Pennsieve stores it, one compressed file. The default is file, except with conformsTo, where it is directory, since a structure is specified in its unpacked form (BIDS expects .ome.zarr folders). See https://github.com/Pennsieve/app-deploy-service/blob/main/docs/app-manifest-folders.md.

conformsTo.description: The folder structure the whole input follows, or that the app writes: a structure id from the Pennsieve format registry with an optional version (bids, bids@1.9), or a link to any other specification (https://…, matched only by the same link). A list nests structures, outermost first: [pennsieve-published-dataset, bids] is a published dataset whose files/ folder is BIDS. The input is always a folder tree with its paths kept; mediaTypes then say what the tree holds, and container how folder-format items in it are given (directory unless set).

placement.description: Where an input's data is placed. root (the default): at the root of INPUT_DIR. subfolder: in its own folder, INPUT_DIR/<name>/, so inputs that would collide (two BIDS trees) stay apart; the name must then be folder-safe (lowercase letters, numbers, dashes). Inputs of different media types can share the root (the app tells them apart by type); inputs that share a type, take any file, or are a layout need their own folders.

required.description: Whether a run must give it something.
